note: Terms module-01 introduces, and the lesson responsible for teaching each. Enforced by scripts/lint-glossary.mjs. Module-01 is the energy-trading module: it carries the highest domain-vocabulary cost in the curriculum and, before 2026-08-22, the ONLY gloss anywhere in 120 lessons (one parenthetical covering hub, MWh, and settled price). Keep ASCII-only.

terms.gloss: A regional point where electricity is bought and sold. Prices are quoted per hub the way fuel prices are quoted per region.
Megawatt-hour: the unit electricity is priced in. Roughly the power an average home uses in a month, so $/MWh is the wholesale price tag.
The final cleared price for the day, after the intraday spikes stop moving. The spike is the drama; the settled price is what the books use.
The grid operator that runs most of Texas. Here it is simply the name of the hub the desk watches.
The team that trades and watches the market. 'The desk' is the group; the analyst and the trader both sit on it.
How much power was actually produced, by source (wind, gas, solar). Generation missing forecast is usually why a price moved.
The gap between two numbers you expected to agree - here, today's price against yesterday's. Computed once and stored, so every later step cites the same figure.
The line that decides routine from escalate. It lives in a policy someone owns, never inside the logic that applies it.
A named, structured object the workflow produces and later steps reuse - market-intake.json, clean-price-data.json. Artifacts are how progress is measured here, not lessons completed.
Upstream is what feeds this step; downstream is what consumes it. The map draws both so you can see what breaks if this step is wrong.
The agreed set of field names and types a record must have. Changing it is a breaking change for everything downstream, which is why it carries a version.
Setting a bad row aside instead of guessing at it or dropping it silently. A quarantined row is visible, countable, and someone's job.
Producing a deliberately reduced output when an input is missing, and saying so on the face of it - rather than producing a confident-looking output built on a hole.
